reason: Both meet the hard requirements, but Response B is more rigorous about the snapshot gate — it explicitly requires 'completed successfully (status = success, not just started)' before any destructive step, whereas Response A's parallel language ('must complete... or be confirmed in-progress and durable') is internally inconsistent and slightly weakens the same safety guarantee. Response B also adds more actionable technical detail (snapshotting to a separate volume when the disk itself is near full, checking WAL/temp volumes separately, post-mitigation data-integrity/checksum verification) that makes it marginally more useful as an actual runbook.
